bug_semantics: A repository-controlled .gitmodules section name is parsed unchanged by sm_name(), assigned to Submodule._name, and, on Git versions using gitfile submodules, joined to <parent git dir>/modules. A name containing ../ components therefore escapes that directory. During submodule initialization, GitPython creates parent directories and clones with --separate-git-dir at the escaped location, allowing a malicious repository whose otherwise tree-validated submodule path is legitimate to create and populate a Git repository at an attacker-chosen filesystem path.
flaw_origin: Commit 503b62bd76ee742bd18a1803dac76266fa8901bc introduced _need_gitfile_submodules() and _module_abspath(), whose modern-Git branch returned os.path.join(parent_repo.git_dir, 'modules', name), and changed update() to use that name-derived path for directory removal and Repo.clone_from(). The already-existing iter_items() flow obtained name by slicing the attacker-controlled .gitmodules section header with sm_name() and performed no validation. This commit created the first name-to-filesystem sink; later commit 67680a0877f01177dc827beb49c83a9174cdb736 refactored cloning into _clone_repo() and added --separate-git-dir but was not the first vulnerable implementation.
ai_marker: No BIC commit-object AI signal. `git cat-file commit 503b62bd76ee742bd18a1803dac76266fa8901bc` shows author and committer Sebastian Thiel <byronimo@gmail.com> and a conventional message ending `Relates #233`; it has no AI Co-Authored-By, Generated-with, Assisted-by, agent marker, or bot identity.
evidence: First-party advisory https://github.com/gitpython-developers/GitPython/security/advisories/GHSA-hmq2-w58f-27jc states affected <=3.1.57 and patched >=3.1.58, identifies sm_name() -> Submodule._name -> _module_abspath() -> _clone_repo(), and records a released-3.1.57 PoC in which name '../../../../../../tmp/gitpython_poc_escaped_root/modules_dir' makes sm.update(init=True) create the escaped repository while core Git rejects the suspicious name.

Run `git show --format=fuller 503b62bd76ee742bd18a1803dac76266fa8901bc -- git/objects/submodule/base.py`: the non-merge commit adds `_module_abspath`, returning `os.path.join(parent_repo.git_dir, 'modules', name)` for Git >=1.8, and changes update() from its checkout-path destination to `self._module_abspath(self.repo, self.path, self.name)` before cloning. `git show 503b62bd76ee742bd18a1803dac76266fa8901bc:git/objects/submodule/base.py` lines around iter_items show `n = sm_name(sms)`, tree lookup by the separate `path`, then `sm._name = n`; util.py shows sm_name merely returns `section[11:-1]`.

Direct-parent proof: `git cat-file -p 503b62bd76ee742bd18a1803dac76266fa8901bc` names sole parent a9a5414300a245b6e93ea4f39fbca792c3ec753f. `git grep -n -E '_module_abspath|separate_git_dir|git_dir.*modules|modules.*name' a9a5414300a245b6e93ea4f39fbca792c3ec753f -- git/objects/submodule` returns no matches, and the parent's update() uses `join_path_native(self.repo.working_tree_dir, self.path)` and clones there. Thus the immediate parent lacks the vulnerable name-derived module path.

Origin cross-check: `git log -L 304,313:git/objects/submodule/base.py 6e61b1d3bdcd2d9b81bac4eb4d17c18b270e5787` traces _module_abspath through formatting/type-only edits back to its addition in 503b62bd76ee742bd18a1803dac76266fa8901bc; `git log --all --reverse -S'_module_abspath' -- git/objects/submodule/base.py` likewise identifies 503b62bd76ee742bd18a1803dac76266fa8901bc as the first substantive addition. The commit has one parent and is not a move, revert, release commit, merge, or squash aggregate.

Release-boundary proof: `git describe --contains --tags 503b62bd76ee742bd18a1803dac76266fa8901bc` returns `0.3.6~35`; `git merge-base --is-ancestor 503b62bd76ee742bd18a1803dac76266fa8901bc 0.3.5` exits 1, while `git tag --contains 503b62bd76ee742bd18a1803dac76266fa8901bc --sort=version:refname` begins at 0.3.6 and includes every maintained line through 3.1.57. History therefore narrows the source introduction to release 0.3.6 even though the advisory expresses the vulnerable upper bound as <=3.1.57.

Fix proof: `git show e4b8e7d026ca6abb4cf604f8e77093432ce23c06 -- git/objects/submodule/base.py test/test_submodule.py` adds _validated_name(), rejects empty, rooted/drive-qualified and `..` names, validates before filesystem operations, and adds an exact traversal regression asserting no escaped directory is created. Mainline merge 2212c6396dac0b2a8f03fc2e6708c72b6f363cc9 has e4b8e7d026ca6abb4cf604f8e77093432ce23c06 as its second parent. Follow-up 4299c990e1ca21896f9485277caf7bb0ae5b404c moves validation ahead of the legacy branch. `git tag --contains` places both direct commits first in 3.1.58, and the 3.1.58 changes.rst names GHSA-hmq2-w58f-27jc; 3.1.57 precedes them.

BIC-only AI check: `git cat-file commit 503b62bd76ee742bd18a1803dac76266fa8901bc` prints tree 4e703edaa7a63f3ab33c28dbf53af5ccced337c2, parent a9a5414300a245b6e93ea4f39fbca792c3ec753f, human author/committer Sebastian Thiel <byronimo@gmail.com>, and no trailers or AI/bot identity. AI markers on the 2026 fix are deliberately excluded from the verdict.
reasoning: The vulnerability begins at the first commit that replaces the tree-constrained checkout path with a separate Git-directory path containing the unchecked .gitmodules name. That is 503b62bd76ee742bd18a1803dac76266fa8901bc, not the later _clone_repo refactor. Its sole parent directly lacks both the path constructor and any name-derived filesystem sink. The direct security patch is e4b8e7d026ca6abb4cf604f8e77093432ce23c06, landed on main through 2212c6396dac0b2a8f03fc2e6708c72b6f363cc9 and released, with a legacy-branch follow-up, in 3.1.58. Because the 2015 BIC commit object has a human identity and no AI disclosure or bot signal, the required BIC-only judgment is NOT_AI regardless of AI assistance disclosed on the 2026 fix.
